findings.title: Half the actionable pill face is a dead click zone with a pointer cursor
findings.evidence: Live hit-test: with a grounded suggestion + peek open, click at x=60 (label area) dismisses the card and sends next_suggestion.feedback accept over ws:8765; clicks at x=140 and x=200 hit .vmx-pill-wave__bar inside the waveform mount which boot() tags data-no-drag (index.ts:1987), and pillPeekHandlePrimaryActionClick (index.ts:989-1005) rejects any [data-no-drag] target. Meanwhile pill.css:693-695 sets cursor:pointer on the WHOLE .pill__row when data-actionable, so ~140px of the 280px face promises a click that silently does nothing.
findings.fix_sketch: Exempt the waveform from the click guard (it is aria-hidden decoration, not a control): either drop data-no-drag from waveEl (it already sits below the drag strip) or add ".vmx-pill-wave" to an allowlist in pillPeekHandlePrimaryActionClick so the no-drag check only blocks real controls (buttons/chips/card).

findings.title: The 'next ready' notch is 100% clipped — an instrument that can never paint
findings.evidence: Measured in the live page: notch boundingRect.top=44 == pill height 44, height 3, clippedPx=3, .pill overflow:hidden — and the native window is also 44px collapsed (pill_window.rs:94), so the notch + its 4 ready/glint keyframes (pill-next-notch-ready-a/b, glint-a/b) never render a single pixel in browser OR overlay. The comment calls it 'the tiny more-below signal'; it is dead weight shipping as if it signals.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the notch INSIDE the 44px face (e.g. top: 39px so its 3px fits above the bottom edge), or grow set_pill_height by ~4px when data-has-next, or delete the notch + keyframes and let the dot ring (data-intel=knows) be the single 'next ready' signal.

findings.title: Camelot numerics render rose, not gold — --amber is aliased to --brand
findings.evidence: Screenshot 05-expand-negative shows deck chip 'a · 8a · 124' with '8a' in rose. .vmx-deck-chip__key--resolved { color: var(--amber) } and tokens.css:288 defines --amber: var(--brand) (#FFA5DF rose). The pink mock contract renders .camelot-chip in var(--gold) with gold-glow (mock lines 707-731) — gold is reserved for exactly heat/Camelot numerics. The pill spends rose on the one glyph the contract says is gold, and the only gold on the surface is misapplied to the peek cue-rail gradient (next-suggestion.ts:246, a timing meter, not a numeric).
findings.fix_sketch: Change .vmx-deck-chip__key--resolved to color: var(--gold) (+ optional text-shadow var(--gold-glow)); swap the cue-rail gradient to brand-only so gold stays Camelot/heat-exclusive. Audit the 'gold only for the XP heat number' comment in next-suggestion.ts (no XP number is ever rendered).

findings.title: Rose budget blown: 5+ simultaneous rose accents per reaction vs One-Rose/one-breath
findings.evidence: Screenshot 04-expand-bomb shows in one frame: rose waveform bars (up to 14), rose BOMB lead with triple text-shadow glow, rose receipt rule, rose stage rail (expand::after), rose radial bloom (expand::before + reaction::after), rose-bordered citation chips, rose camelot glyph, plus the rose dot. Collapsed speaking already runs two breathing rose elements (blinking dot pill.css:738-748 + lit bars waveform.ts:71-77). The mock's law is one rose accent breathing at a time; the pill's own comments still claim a 'four reserved amber accents' budget, which itself predates the rose contract.
findings.fix_sketch: Pick the reaction lead as THE rose element during expand: demote receipt rule and stage rail to silk (they already have silk variants for clean/mid), keep chips glass-edge, and make the dot yield (silk) while the waveform is lit during speaking.

findings.title: Glyphs below the ink-20 text floor: silk-40 (and silk-40 × 0.72) body-info text at 9-10px
findings.evidence: silk-40 composited over --glass-3 ≈ #706D6F ≈ 3.4:1 contrast — below the --ink-20 (#8A858A ≈ 4.9:1) floor — used for load-bearing info glyphs: the honest 'unknown' key/bpm in deck chips (10px mono), the 'decks · unknown' fallback chip further dimmed to opacity 0.72 (pill.css:1804-1814, visible in shot 14 as barely-there), the 'next' micro-label and why-text at 9px (next-suggestion.ts:132,212). The honest-null read is the anti-slop centerpiece; it ships below the floor the contract sets.
findings.fix_sketch: Raise the floor: silk-65 for unknown key/bpm and the fallback chip (drop the extra 0.72 opacity), silk-65 for .vmx-next-card__why; keep silk-40 only for true decoration (aria-hidden hairlines).

findings.title: Peek primary action promises 'load suggestion' but nothing is loaded
findings.evidence: nextSuggestionPrimaryActionAriaLabel appends 'activate to load suggestion' and the card is role=button; activating it sends next_suggestion.feedback accept (verified on the wire) and the card vanishes with zero confirmation. vibemix cannot load a track into the DJ software — record_feedback (ws_bus.py:1154-1166) pins the pick and feeds the taste loop. The accessible name promises an action the system cannot perform, and the visible result (card silently disappears) reads as dismissal, not acceptance.
findings.fix_sketch: Rename the action to what it does: 'activate to accept pick' / 'pin this next'. Add a one-breath acknowledgment (e.g. echo label 'PINNED' for 1.8s reusing the reactionEcho path) so accept is distinguishable from dismiss.

findings.title: ~100 literal cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) duplicating the existing --ease-brand token (+ one stray second bezier)
findings.evidence: tokens.css:250 defines --ease-brand: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); pill.css inlines that exact literal ~100 times (lines 110-2997) and introduces a one-off cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) at pill.css:1750 for the receipt draw. findings.fix_sketch: sed the literal to var(--ease-brand) (or it can't be used inside animation shorthand? it can — custom properties work in transition/animation timing position via var()); fold 0.22,1,0.36,1 into --ease-brand or add a named --ease-draw token; pull decorative-only animations toward the 150-250ms band.

findings.title: Six dead [data-feedback] selectors — state hook never set by any pill TS

findings.fix_sketch: Delete the [data-feedback] terms from the six selectors (or wire the attribute if a feedback-ack state is planned per the 'PINNED' echo above).

findings.title: Keyboard re-activation trap: focused pill ignores Enter for a fresh suggestion until blur/refocus
findings.evidence: Reproduced live: accept a pick (closePeekToRoot(true) sets peek=false, root keeps focus) → a NEW suggestion arrives on the wire → press Enter → nothing (card stays hidden, no send; verified sent array unchanged). peek only re-opens on focusin/pointerenter, and an already-focused root never re-fires focusin, so a keyboard-only operator must Tab away and back to act on the next pick.
findings.fix_sketch: In the bus listener, when a suggestion with a NEW render key arrives while document.activeElement === root, re-arm peek (state = setPeek(state, true)) — mirrors what pointer users get from still-hovering.

findings.title: Copy register wobble: 'DJ KNOWS' / 'COHOST' / 'LIT AFF' on the collapsed face
findings.evidence: Hover with a grounded pick flips the state label to 'DJ KNOWS' (screenshot 10); expand relabels the face 'COHOST' (the rest of the product says Sven); echo labels surface backend slugs as 'LIT AFF' / 'NEG' (move-grade-vocabulary.json). findings.fix_sketch: Pick one register for the face label: keep the state words (IDLE/LISTENING/SPEAKING) + 'NEXT READY' instead of 'DJ KNOWS', 'SVEN' instead of 'COHOST', and map lit_aff/negative to spoken-register labels ('LIT', 'HOLD') in PILL_MOVE_GRADE_VOCABULARY labels.

findings.title: Ring placement rides a hand-guessed 12-element percentage map, not real element positions — precision the voice implies but the instrument does not have
findings.evidence: READ: COORD_MAP is hand-mapped to 'djay Pro 5.x default layout @ 1920x1080' with a comment asserting 'proportions hold' on other sizes; query_element_bounds() multiplies those fixed percentages into whatever window rect Quartz returns (djay_ax.rs:86-105). djay's layout is adaptive (library pane, 2/4-deck view, collapsed EQ), so the same percentages land on different controls. When Sven says 'your low EQ on deck A' and the ring draws around the gain knob, the product's own grounding promise is broken by its pointing finger. The AX-precise path is explicitly deferred ('Plan 24-03 will replace this IF the spike verdict comes back PASS' — verdict still pending). Honest mitigations exist: djay-absent/unknown-id/degenerate-rect all no-op rather than draw a wrong ring (overlay.rs:46-49).
findings.fix_sketch: Until the AX spike passes, shrink the claim to match the instrument: highlight at deck granularity (one rect per deck half, which the percentage map CAN guarantee) instead of per-knob, or gate per-knob rings behind a verified-layout check (compare djay window aspect/size against the calibration assumption and fall back to the deck rect when it deviates).

findings.title: One-off motion curve + warm-white sheen literals inlined in overlay.html while tokens.css already ships the vocabulary
findings.evidence: READ: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) is hardcoded 3x (.ring, .scan--x, .scan--y) while tokens.css:251 defines --ease-brand: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) — a forked easing vocabulary that will rot silently when the brand curve shifts. Same pattern for material sheen: rgba(255, 251, 244, 0.26/0.34/0.42) and rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.46) are inlined although tokens.css:325-328 ships the exact warm-white specular family as --lg-spec-hi/--lg-rim-light. Contract rule 2: any hardcoded hex/cubic-bezier outside tokens.css is drift. Notably the COLOR layer got this right (VIS-02 fixed the #f59e0b literal; ring resolves --amber→--brand rose, screenshot-verified) — the motion/sheen layer was missed in the same sweep.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the 3 bezier literals with var(--ease-brand) (or add a dedicated --ease-aperture token to tokens.css if the 0.22/1/0.36/1 feel is deliberate); point the sheen rgba()s at the --lg-spec-*/--lg-rim-light ladder, adding alpha steps to tokens.css if the existing ones are too faint.

findings.title: prefers-reduced-motion rule for .ring is a literal no-op — reduced-motion users still get the full scale-breathing ring
findings.evidence: READ: the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block sets `.ring { animation-name: focus-aperture; }` — that IS the animation already assigned at line 71, so the rule changes nothing; the scale 0.985→1→1.012 breath still plays. Only the scan sweeps are genuinely stilled (animation: none, static opacity 0.16). The dangling no-op reads like an unfinished intent to swap in a reduced keyframe set (fade-only, no transform). Note a pure `animation: none` would be wrong too — base state is opacity:0, the ring would never appear.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a second keyframe set (focus-aperture-reduced: opacity-only, no transform) and point the reduced-motion rule at it; delete the no-op as-is if the breath is deemed acceptable.

findings.title: Scan crosshair + tick rails + beads are decorative HUD theater on a state cue
findings.evidence: SAW (ring-amber-default.png, ring-waveform-size.png): beyond the corner ring (which IS the state — 'look here'), the window animates a sweeping horizontal+vertical scanline crosshair, repeating tick rails top/bottom, and two glowing beads. The sweep travels for the full 1300ms default. Contract rule 3: motion conveys state, not decoration — the crosshair sweep conveys nothing the ring doesn't. In its defense it is the surface's only breath (one-breath rule arguably satisfied), it self-extinguishes, and reduced-motion stills it; but stacked with drop-shadow glow on every layer it reads tactical-HUD, a register apart from the pink mock's forged-obsidian quiet.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep ring + corners (the state), drop or radically fade the scan sweep and beads (opacity ≤0.12, or remove); keep rails only at waveform-scale windows where they read as measurement, not garnish.

findings.title: Surface still speaks 'amber / CDJ Whisper v5' internally while shipping rose — stale vocabulary across 3 layers
findings.evidence: SAW: ring renders rose #FFA5DF-family (tokens.css:288 re-points --amber→--brand), matching the pink contract — visual is CORRECT. READ: every layer of the chain still names it amber: overlay.html comments cite 'CDJ Whisper v5 amber' and 'mocks use #ff8a3d' (a retired mock), Python's wire constant is OVERLAY_COLOR='amber', the schema $comment promises 'an amber ring'. Zero user-visible copy on this surface (aria-hidden, no text), so this is internal-naming drift only — but the next engineer reading 'amber' in three places will reintroduce #ff8a3d in good faith.
findings.fix_sketch: Sweep the comments to 'brand rose (via --amber alias)'; consider renaming the wire value amber→brand with a compat alias in TOKEN_FOR_KEY (overlay-runtime.ts:24-32 already makes this a one-line addition).

findings.title: Verdict headline calls chapters "TRACKS" — lying instrument
findings.evidence: SAW (05-mock-populated.png): gold headline "5 TRACKS · 47M IN THE MIX". READ: renderVerdictLine(tldrPanelEl, buildVerdictText(chapters.length, totalDurationS)) — buildVerdictText (tldr-player.ts:117-121) labels its first arg "N TRACKS", but the caller passes the CHAPTER count. Backend chapters.py:_is_break_event breaks on TRACK_CHANGE *and* PHASE/LAYER_ARRIVAL/MIX_MOVE/KAAN_SPOKE (≥30s gap), so chapter count > track count on any real set. A 3-track set with phase movement will proudly read "9 TRACKS". The component's own docstring promises "no invented numbers" — this invents one.
findings.fix_sketch: Plumb the real track count: session-loaded frame (or chapter kind=="track"/TRACK_CHANGE-origin chapters only) → count those; or change the copy to the truthful noun ("5 CHAPTERS" / "5 MOMENTS"). Cheapest honest fix: chapters.filter(c => c.kind === "track"|| originates from TRACK_CHANGE).length, falling back to the duration-only verdict when unknown.

findings.title: Chapter sidebar is a dead control — clicks dispatch an event nobody consumes
findings.evidence: READ: chapter buttons dispatch CustomEvent("chapter-selected") with {id, start, citation_event_id}. grep across src/ shows the ONLY listener is the unit test (chapter-list.spec.ts:50); debrief-window.ts wires citation-click, moment-feedback-click and region-clicked but never chapter-selected. SAW (07-mock-chapter-click.png): clicking "00:00 warm pressure" changes nothing — no seek, no timeline highlight, no readout change. The buttons have full hover/focus styling (rose border, translateX(2px)) so they promise interaction; the entire left rail (~320px of the layout) does nothing when clicked, in both real and mock mode.
findings.fix_sketch: In debrief-window.ts add chaptersEl.addEventListener("chapter-selected", e => { highlight matching .vmx-debrief-region (reuse the deep-link path: dispatch vmx-debrief-deeplink with {eventId: detail.citation_event_id, timestampS: detail.start}) and/or client.sendCitationTooltipRequest(detail.citation_event_id); }). The deep-link machinery in timeline.ts already does scroll+pulse — one dispatch wires it.

findings.title: False "Debrief crashed unexpectedly" verdict during normal sidecar boot (warming ≠ fault)
findings.evidence: SAW (03-fake-session.png): with 8766 not yet bound, the red banner "Debrief crashed unexpectedly. Try reopening." appears within ~2.5s of load. READ: ws.onerror dispatches CustomEvent("error", {detail: rawWsEvent}); debrief-window.ts:163-175 maps ANY "error" event through detail?.reason ?? "sidecar_crashed" — a raw WebSocket Event has no .reason, so every transient connect failure renders the crash verdict. This bypasses the carefully built 120s RECONNECT_BUDGET_MS (ws-client.ts:52) and the 10s "Sven is still putting your debrief together" grace (debrief-window.ts:180-187) — the code's own comments say the sidecar binds 8766 late on every first run. Same disease as Invariant #5: an expected in-between state declared a fault.
findings.fix_sketch: Don't funnel transport onerror into the banner channel: rename the raw dispatch to "ws-error" (or drop it — onclose already drives _scheduleReconnect), so showErrorBanner only fires on (a) schema ipc.debrief.error frames and (b) the synthetic {reason:"sidecar_crashed"} emitted after the 120s budget genuinely exhausts (ws-client.ts:128-134).

findings.title: Cold/empty state: skeletons claim perpetual work that contradicts the terminal error, and teach nothing
findings.evidence: SAW (01-cold-no-session.png, 02-cold-after-7s.png): with no session, banner says "That recording can't be opened…" while all three panels keep claiming activity forever: "Listening back...", "Generating voiced summary…", "Generating drills…" (note even the ellipsis glyph is inconsistent: ASCII '...' vs '…'). READ: debrief-window.ts:57-60 shows the invalid_session_dir branch only raises the banner — skeleton copy is never swapped to a terminal state. Timeline empty copy is "No regions to render." (timeline.ts:48) — internal nouns ("regions", "render"), no path forward. Empty states neither teach ("finish a set and your review lands here") nor stop lying about progress.
findings.fix_sketch: On any terminal error (invalid_session_dir, budget-exhausted crash), replace the three skeletons with quiet resolved copy ("Nothing to listen back to yet."). Rewrite timeline empty state to teach: "Play a set with the co-host live and the timeline builds itself here." Normalize ellipses to one glyph.

findings.title: Gold spent on non-heat numerics — verdict line breaks the gold quarantine
findings.evidence: SAW: "5 TRACKS · 47M IN THE MIX" rendered in gold (#e8c47a) with gold-glow text-shadow — the largest warm element on the surface. findings.fix_sketch: Re-tone .vmx-debrief-verdict to the rose ladder (color: var(--brand-glow); text-shadow brand-40) or ink-primary mono — keep gold for a real heat/Camelot stat if the verdict ever carries one (e.g. peak energy delta).

findings.title: 27 raw color literals in debrief.css, including three RETIRED-palette values
findings.evidence: READ: 27 hardcoded rgba color literals. Worst offenders: rgba(214,207,199,…) at :48, :65, :243, :698 — that's the RETIRED v5 silk #d6cfc7 (tokens.css:16 says silk was promoted to ink #F2EFF1; --silk-025 exists and is used elsewhere in the same file, so the texture grids mix two whites). rgba(255,197,107,0.1) at :1299 (drill-learn hover) — a retired v5 amber-orange that matches NO current token (gold is 232,196,122). rgba(212,65,58,…) at :1370/:1374 — error red bypassing --danger/--led-fault. Plus ~20 rgba(255,165,223,…) literals duplicating the --brand alpha ladder (e.g. :63-65, :73-74, :452-453, :849, :963-977, :988-990, :1014, :1616-1617).

findings.title: TL;DR meta line clipped mid-glyph at 1440x900 — player well too short for its content

findings.title: Evidence tooltip is never anchored — opens at the document tail, not at the clicked chip
findings.evidence: READ: showCitationTooltip(container, payload, anchor?) only sets left/top when anchor is passed (citation-tooltip.ts:41-44). The sole production caller — the citation-tooltip ws listener — calls showCitationTooltip(tooltip, detail) with NO anchor, for both drill-chip clicks and timeline region clicks. #vmx-debrief-tooltip is position:absolute (debrief.css:1417) as the last child of the root, so the "evidence receipt" materializes at the bottom of the document flow, potentially below the fold, nowhere near what the user clicked. The grounding receipt — the product's trust centerpiece — plays hide and seek.
findings.fix_sketch: Capture the click position in the citation-click / region-clicked dispatches (detail: {citation, x: rect.right, y: rect.top}), stash as pendingAnchor, and pass it when the citation-tooltip frame returns; clamp to viewport.

findings.title: Noun chaos: chapters/regions/TRACKS for one object; TL;DR/voiced summary/recap for another; Debrief vs review across surfaces
findings.evidence: SAW on one screen: sidebar header "CHAPTERS", timeline HUD chip "5 regions", gold verdict "5 TRACKS" — three nouns for the same five objects, simultaneously visible. The recap artifact: panel title "TL;DR" (debrief.html:43), skeleton "Generating voiced summary…" (:45), meta "74s recap" (tldr-player.ts:46), error copy says both "voiced summary" (error-banner.ts:24) and "voiced recap" (:28). Cross-surface: the in-shell DebriefDock calls the whole thing "review" ("review dock", "next review", "Open review", "review ready" — DebriefDock.ts:453, 470, 651, 616) while this window titles itself "Debrief".
findings.fix_sketch: Pick one noun per concept and sweep: chapters (kill "regions" in readout + empty copy; verdict per P0 fix), "recap" for the voiced artifact (rename TL;DR panel title — it's also internet jargon), and align dock+window on either "review" or "debrief" everywhere.

findings.title: Copy-law violations: em dash in working banner; port numbers and protocol jargon in user-facing errors
findings.evidence: READ: showWorkingBanner renders "Sven is still putting your debrief together — the first pass can take a minute." (em dash, banned in UI copy). REASON_COPY ships internals: "Port 8766 is already taken by another process. Close the other debrief window and reopen." (:29-30), "Received an unknown message kind from the backend." (:31-32), "Its location doesn't match the expected layout." (:20-21 — developer-speak; SAW it verbatim in 01-cold-no-session.png). Also debrief.html:6 ships <title>Debrief —</title> (dangling em dash, visible until JS overwrites it).
findings.fix_sketch: Em dash → period or comma ("…together. The first pass can take a minute."). port_in_use → "Another review window is already open. Close it and reopen this one." unknown_kind → "Something arrived I don't understand. Try reopening." invalid_session_dir → "I can't find that set's recording. Open the review from the deck after a session." Fix the static title.

findings.title: Moment-feedback buttons: "OFF" reads as a power toggle, choice can't be unpressed, no sent/failed state

findings.title: Invisible, unnamed, keyboard-focusable RESTART button sits on the live deck at all times
findings.evidence: VERIFIED LIVE (shot 16 probe): in running/live mode (data-mode="") `button.vmx-live__s--fault` accepted focus with computed opacity:0, textContent "", tabIndex 0. The CSS only gates pointer-events (lines 425-426, 438), which does not block keyboard. Tab from STOP lands on a zero-width empty button; the global *:focus-visible (tokens.css:610) draws around nothing. Enter dispatches click -> cohost.onRetry -> restart_sidecar (render-loop.ts:46-51): an invisible control that restarts the co-host mid-set, with no accessible name when no fault is active.
findings.fix_sketch: In applyState, when mode !== "fault" set liveFault.disabled = true (or tabIndex = -1) and aria-hidden="true"; re-enable + set aria-label="restart co-host" only in fault mode — mirror the setInputDown() pattern already used for status-row inputs (SessionLayout.ts:2246).

findings.title: "audio input dropped" fault state is dead-wired — no backend producer can ever fire it
findings.evidence: faultInput() flips the deck to fault only on status.livekit === "down", but grep across src/vibemix shows NO emitter ever sends livekit="down": ws_bus.py:1510 hardcodes livekit="ok" in the 1Hz tick (comment: "never-fault"), session_loop.py:1695 recheck replies only ok/connecting, wizard.py:620 sends connecting. A real capture loss arrives only as ipc.error audio.capture -> deck notice + armed (ws-bridge.ts:653-662). The deck's primary audio-fault hero (shot 01) is reachable only by injection; if capture silently degrades without the backend self-parking, the deck never shows it.
findings.fix_sketch: Either wire a real capture-health probe into the status tick (livekit="down" when the input stream callback stops delivering), or delete the audio branch from faultInput and route ALL capture loss through the audio.capture notice path so UI vocabulary matches what the wire can actually say.

findings.title: Fault with empty transcript renders a blank hero — failure state with no cause or recovery in the body
findings.evidence: SCREENSHOT 04: fresh session + fault = vast empty void; nowText falls through to "" (`mode === "silent" ? IDLE_HERO_LINE : ""` — fault gets empty string). The only cause indicator is the 10px mono "◂ audio input dropped" top-right; nothing says it is clickable (title tooltip only), no "what do I do now" copy anywhere in the body. This is the documented recurring "blank hero / always broken" failure shape, surviving for the no-transcript case.
findings.fix_sketch: In fault mode with no nowLine, render a grounded fault hero in the dimmed silent treatment: cause + action ("Audio input dropped. Check your capture routing, or tap restart.") — an operating state, not a fabricated reaction, mirroring how IDLE_HERO_LINE handles silent.

findings.title: Idle setup instruction wears the "earlier" ghost-mark — current guidance labeled as prior speech
findings.evidence: SCREENSHOT 05: at silent idle the readiness ACTION line ("BLACKHOLE 2CH: SEND DJ APP TO A MULTI-OUTPUT/AGGREGATE...") renders into ghost g1 (lines 1875-1879), and `.vmx-ghost--g1:not(:empty)::before` unconditionally prefixes "earlier" — so the screen literally reads "EARLIER BLACKHOLE 2CH: SEND DJ APP...". The mark means prior co-host speech; this instruction was never spoken. A lying label on the exact line that teaches the empty state.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `.vmx-session[data-mode="silent"] .vmx-ghost--g1::before { content: none; }` (the idle path is the only one that writes non-transcript text into g1), or give idle lines their own mark ("set up").

findings.title: Voice-engine-down is labeled "muted" — the UI blames the user for an engine failure
findings.evidence: Backend: live_voice_muted = not _local_voice_ready_for_status() (__main__.py:2089) — wire voice="muted" (ws_bus.py:1514) means Chatterbox NOT READY, not user-muted. Deck renders it as idle note "Voice muted." (line 2116), red status-row word "voice" with aria "voice status muted" (line 2263). A user whose voice engine failed reads that they muted it; the mute button shows unpressed "mute" simultaneously, and toggling it cannot recover an engine-down.
findings.fix_sketch: Split the wire enum (voice: ok | muted | down) — backend already knows the difference (config muted vs _local_voice_ready_for_status). Until then, copy "Voice not ready." when status.muted is false but voice==="muted" (the contradiction is detectable UI-side).

findings.title: BPM=0 would print "0.0" as a measured value (latent lying instrument)

findings.fix_sketch: `const bpmMissing = bpmValue == null || bpmValue <= 0;` — one-line guard matching the bpmPeriodMs guard already in ws-bridge.applySnapshot (line 392).

findings.title: Debrief / Learn / Library windows open platform-white before the dark void paints (white flash on a dark app)

On macOS the WKWebView canvas defaults to WHITE until first CSS paint, so every 'open Debrief/Learn/Library' pops a white frame on an all-dark (#1A1618) app. The fix already exists elsewhere and was not copied: main window uses transparent:true (tauri.conf.json5:54) + NSVisualEffectView vibrancy applied in setup (main.rs:57/178); pill/mascot/overlay use .transparent(true) (pill_window.rs:217, mascot_window.rs:103, overlay.rs:73). Learn compounds it: learn.html mounts ALL content via JS, so even after CSS the first ~150ms is a featureless black void (SAW: learn-50ms.png pure black vs learn-150ms.png full UI) — white → black void → UI, a three-step boot flash.
